text.p: Compaq Computer Corp on Thursday said it introduced at aggressive prices 13 new Deskpro personal computers aimed at the corporate market designed using Compaq "build-to-order" manufacturing strategy.
The new Deskpro PCs, the Deskpro 2000 line, start at prices of $1,199 to $1,899. The Deskpro 4000 models range in prices from $1,389 to $2,089.

At the same time, Compaq cut prices across the board on its older Deskpro 2000, 4000 and 6000 lines from two to 22 percent. For example, the entry level price of a Deskpro 2000 PC with an Intel 166 MHz Pentium chip will now be $999.
Compaq said that it has already shipped 100,000 units designed using its build-to-order manufacturing method.
Compaq's Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason said that by the end of the year, he expects 100 percent of Compaq's products to be manufactured by its build-to-order process.

Ahead of a press conference to introduce the new models, Mason said that contrary to some analysts' beliefs, Compaq's gross profit margins will not be hurt by its new manufacturing strategy and lower pricing.
"I think it will help profits," Mason said. "Our whole program is designed at improving profitability."

Mason said he could not forecast Compaq's future gross profit margins, but he said that he is comfortable with the current profit margin of 25.3 percent of revenues, which it reported earlier Thursday in its second quarter results.
Mason also said he is comfortable with Wall Street analysts' estimates of $1.53 a share for the third quarter.

Compaq's new line of PCs includes seven value-oriented Deskpro 2000 models with Intel Corp Pentium with MMX technologies, with speeds ranging from 166MHz to 233MHz and hard drives as big as 3.2 gigabytes.
The six new Deskpro 4000 models, geared more toward networked environments are available with similar processers and memory, Compaq said.

Older models of the Deskpro 6000 models, designed for sophisticated networked environments, were reduced in price. The company said the Deskpro 6000 with a 200MHz Pentium Pro processor, 2.1 gigabyte hard drive and 32 megabytes of memory was reduced to $2,419, a nine percent reduction.
